ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r1.claim: The verb’s subject is unstated, but the following verses identify the Prophet as the one who frowned.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r1.anchor: the succeeding verses that the Prophet (sws) is its subject

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r3.speaker: some narratives
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r3.claim: Some narratives describe the Prophet speaking with Quraysh leaders when Ibn Umm Maktūm entered without recognizing the meeting’s delicate nature; the Prophet disliked the interruption.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r3.anchor: It is mentioned in some narratives that one day the Prophet (sws) was talking to one of the leaders of the Quraysh

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r4.claim: The Prophet’s displeasure was not due to the man’s poverty or blindness; he may have feared losing a chance to persuade Quraysh leaders, who might reject a gathering of poor companions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r4.anchor: This dislike on the part of the Prophet (sws) of course could not have been because he was poor or blind

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r1.claim: Quraysh leaders objected that the Prophet’s companions were poor and destitute, treating this as evidence against his prophethood.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r1.anchor: his companions were the poverty-stricken and the destitute. They regarded this to be an argument against his prophethood

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r2.claim: The Prophet may also have feared that arrogant leaders would disrespect his dear companion, causing still greater distress.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r2.anchor: he feared that these leaders being inebriated with their superiority

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r3.claim: God used the accidental incident to teach the Prophet to focus on companions eager for reform, rather than pampering indifferent people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r3.anchor: used by the Almighty for the instruction and education of the Prophet (sws)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r1.claim: The unnamed addressee leaves readers wondering who the incident concerns, while “you know” indicates that the Prophet is being addressed and neglects his own flock for lost sheep.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r1.anchor: shows that this incident relates to the Prophet (sws)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r2.claim: The initial lack of a specified addressee reassures readers; naming the Prophet would suggest the rebuke was for rudeness toward a blind man, which was not its cause.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r2.anchor: had the addressee been specified, this rebuke would have become very severe

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r3.claim: The later direct address identifies the rebuke’s occasion: the Prophet exceeded his duty through zeal, as prophets can overreach from devotion; Moses likewise arrived early at Ṭūr from eagerness to please God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r3.anchor: this rebuke was not because the Prophet (sws) was in anyway slack in fulfilling an obligation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r1.claim: The Prophet’s devotion to persuading Quraysh leaders led him to neglect his own comfort and risk leaving little time to teach poor believers; he had assumed more than God required.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r1.anchor: he had taken much more upon himself than the responsibility that was imposed upon him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r3.claim: The apparent admonition to the Prophet indirectly condemns unworthy Quraysh leaders and redirects his efforts toward poor Muslims who had embraced faith.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r3.anchor: the admonition sounded in these verses which apparently seems directed at the Prophet (sws) is actually directed at the unworthy leaders of the Qurasyh

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r4.claim: The Prophet was corrected for taking on more than his assigned responsibility, not for neglecting it; 26:3 offers another affectionate admonition of this kind.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r4.anchor: the Prophet (sws) has not been checked for being irresponsible in any manner

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r5.claim: Poor Muslims who fear God are Islam’s real asset, unlike affluent people whose hearts lack God-fearingness, so the Prophet should prioritize them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r5.anchor: the real asset of Islam are the poor Muslims who are instilled with the fear of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p178/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p178/r1.speaker: Far āhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p178/r1.claim: Farāhī’s shepherd analogy shows that an apparent rebuke of a conscientious shepherd is actually aimed at a foolish lost sheep; likewise, Quraysh are indirectly rebuked while the Prophet is treated affectionately.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p178/r1.anchor: Im ām Ham īd al-D īn Far āhī in his exegesis on S ūrah ‘Abas

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p179/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p179/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p179/r2.claim: Any reproach in the address is affectionate and means the Prophet assumed more responsibility than was assigned to him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p179/r2.anchor: if there is an element of rebuke in this address it is affection-oriented

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p406/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p406/r2.speaker: الجمهور؛ زيد بن علي، الحسن، أبو عمران الجوني، عيسى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p406/r2.claim: The majority lighten ب in عبس; Zayd doubles it, and some read the following hamza as an interrogative with lengthening or two hamzas.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p406/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور عبس مخففا، أن بهمزة واحدة وزيد بن علي: بشد الباء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39/r1.claim: Sūrat ʿAbasa is also called al-Ṣākhkha, al-Safara, and in some books Sūrat al-Aʿmā; it is Meccan by agreement and has 42 verses in the Hijazi and Kufan counts, 41 in Basran, and 40 in Syrian and the first Medinan count.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39/r1.anchor: وتسمى سورة الصاخة وسورة السفرة وسميت في غير كتاب سورة الأعمى وهي مكية بلا خلاف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39/r2.claim: After the preceding surah says the Prophet warns those who fear the Hour, this surah distinguishes those who benefit from warning from those who do not.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39/r2.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه فيما قبلها إنما أنت منذر من يخشاها ذكر عز وجل في هذه من ينفعه الإنذار

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.claim: The surah explains the call to warn those who fear by using resurrection to purify receptive hearts; human creation and the cycle of food prove God’s power, making rejection astonishing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.anchor: بأن المراد الأعظم تزكية القابل للخشية بالتخويف بالقيامة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r3.claim: The name ʿAbasa points to the surah’s lesson, while al-Ṣākhkhah and al-Bākhkhah evoke the blast’s destructive force.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r3.anchor: واسمها عبس هو الدال على ذلك بتأمل آياته وتدبر فواصله وغاياته ، وكذا الصاخة النافخة بشرها وشررها والباخة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r4.claim: The basmala describes God as powerful and wise, universally granting existence and guidance, and completing His favor specifically for His allies.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r4.anchor: الذي له القدرة البالغة والحكمة الباهرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p103/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p103/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p103/r1.claim: Opening with two verbs whose pronouns lack an antecedent creates suspense; later references to the blind man and the rich man clarify the people and event.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p103/r1.anchor: افتتاح هذه السورة بفعلين متحملين لضمير لا معاد له في الكلام تشويق لما سيورد بعدهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p103/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p103/r2.speaker: مالك عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p103/r2.claim: In a mursal report, Ibn Umm Maktum came asking to be brought near while the Prophet addressed a Meccan notable; the opening was revealed when the Prophet turned toward the notable. Al-Tirmidhi transmits a similar report from Urwa via Aisha and grades it hasan gharib.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p103/r2.anchor: وهو ما رواه مالك في ( الموطأ ) مرسلا عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه أنه قال : أنزلت { عبس وتولى } في ابن أم مكتوم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202/r1.claim: Surat ʿAbasa is Meccan according to everyone.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202/r1.anchor: سورة عبس مكية في قول الجميع

STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r1.claim: This is an early Makkan surah, also called al-Ṣākhkhah after verse 33 and al-Safarah after verse 15.
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r1.anchor: an early Makkan sūrah that takes its name from the first sūrah’s word. It is also known as al-Ṣākhkhah

STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r2.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r2.claim: Some connect its opening to 79:45: the Prophet should not focus on indifferent hearers while seekers await guidance.
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r2.anchor: Some maintain that it is related to the previous sūrah by the manner in which the first ten verses reinforce the message of 79:45

STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r3.speaker: ʿĀʾishah
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r3.claim: ʿĀʾishah reports that the passage concerns blind ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm, who repeatedly sought guidance while the Prophet addressed Makkan leaders; the Prophet turned away, and the verses rebuked him.
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r3.anchor: ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet, reported that this sūrah was revealed about ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm

STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r4.claim: Ibn Umm Maktūm was among Islam's first converts and devoted to the Prophet and Quran; afterward the Prophet welcomed him as the one for whom his Lord rebuked him.
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r4.anchor: After the revelation of this sūrah, it is said that the Prophet would greet him by saying

STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r5.claim: Ibn Umm Maktūm was among the first two migrants to Madinah, taught Quran, and shared the call to prayer with Bilāl.
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r5.anchor: Ibn Umm Maktūm was one of the first two people to migrate to Madinah, where he taught the Quran to many people

STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r6.claim: The Prophet sometimes left Madinah in Ibn Umm Maktūm's care; 4:95 is also said to concern his blindness and exemption from campaigns.
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r6.anchor: It is also said that 4:95 was revealed regarding the particular case of Ibn Umm Maktūm

STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r7.claim: Though blind and excused from expeditions, Ibn Umm Maktūm insisted on a battlefield role; after Qādisiyyah he was found dead holding the Muslim standard.
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r7.anchor: After the Battle of Qādisiyyah in 14/636, he was found dead on the battlefield still clutching the standard

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p449/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p449/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p449/r1.claim: Wahidi identifies the blind man as Ibn Umm Maktūm, who interrupted the Prophet’s appeal to Quraysh chiefs for instruction; the Prophet later honored him as the man for whom his Lord reproached him.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p449/r1.anchor: وهو ابن أم مكتوم، وذلك أنه أتى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وهو يناجي عتبة بن ربيعة وأبا جهل بن هشام

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p449/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p449/r2.speaker: عائشة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p449/r2.claim: ʿĀʾisha likewise reports that the passage was revealed when the blind Ibn Umm Maktūm asked the Prophet for guidance while he addressed leading polytheists.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p449/r2.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: أنزل {عبس وتولى} في ابن أم مكتوك الأعمى، أتى إلى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348/r1.claim: Qatāda says Ibn Umm Maktūm came while the Prophet was speaking with Ubayy ibn Khalaf; the Prophet turned away, the verse was revealed, and afterward he honored Ibn Umm Maktūm.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ عبس وتولى ﴾ قال جاء ابن أم مكتوم إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348/r2.claim: Anas ibn Mālik says he saw Ibn Umm Maktūm at al-Qādisiyya wearing armor and carrying a black banner.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348/r2.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة قال أخبرني أنس بن مالك قال رأيته يوم القادسية عليه درع ومعه راية سوداء يعني ابن أم مكتوم

DURR-FULL:v8p415/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r1.claim: The sūra is Meccan and has forty-two verses.

DURR-FULL:v8p415/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that Surat ʿAbasa was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت سورة عبس بمكة

DURR-FULL:v8p415/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r3.speaker: ابن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr gives the same report that Surat ʿAbasa was revealed in Mecca.

DURR-FULL:v8p415/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r4.speaker: أبو وائل
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r4.claim: Abu Waʾil reports that a man from the Banu Asad delegation recited part of the sūra, added his own line about God creating a child, and was told by the Prophet not to add to its sufficient wording.
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r4.anchor: عن أبي وائل: أن وفد بني أسد أتوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: من أنتم

DURR-FULL:v8p415/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r5.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r5.claim: Anas reports that al-ʿAlaʾ ibn Yazid recited ʿAbasa, added a line of his own, and the Prophet stopped him, saying the sūra had ended.
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r5.anchor: عن أنس قال: استأذن العلاء بن يزيد الحضرمي على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأذن له

DURR-FULL:v8p415/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r6.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r6.claim: ʿAʾisha reports that the passage was revealed concerning the blind Ibn Umm Maktum, who sought guidance while the Prophet was addressing a prominent polytheist.
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r6.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: أنزل سورة عبس وتولى في ابن أم مكتوم والأعمى أتى رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.claim: In another account, ʿAʾisha says the Prophet was addressing Quraysh leaders including Abu Jahl and ʿUtba when Ibn Umm Maktum came; the Prophet turned away, and the quoted passage was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في مجلس من ناس من وجوه قريش منهم أبو جهل بن هشام وعتبة بن ربيعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r1.claim: The standard title is Sūrat ʿAbasa; Ibn al-ʿArabī also calls it Sūrat Ibn Umm Maktūm, a title Ibn ʿĀshūr found nowhere else.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r1.anchor: سميت هذه الصورة في المصاحف وكتب التفسير وكتب السنة ( سورة عبس )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r2.speaker: الخفاجي والعيني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r2.claim: Al-Khafaji calls it Sūrat al-Ṣākhkhah; al-ʿAyni calls it Sūrat al-Safara or Sūrat al-Aʿmā, names taken from distinctive wording or the story’s protagonist.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r2.anchor: وقال الخفاجي : تسمى ( سورة الصاخة ) . وقال العيني في ( شرح صحيح البخاري ) تسمى ( سورة السفرة ) ، وتسمى سورة ( الأعمى )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r3.claim: Al-Suyuti’s list of suras with multiple names omits this sura, which he lists under the name ʿAbasa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r3.anchor: ولم يذكرها صاحب ( الإتقان ) في السور التي لها أكثر من اسم وهو عبس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r4.claim: The sura is Meccan by consensus.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r5.speaker: ابن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r5.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says scholars had not established which passages were Meccan or Medinan, nor the time Ibn Umm Maktūm became Muslim.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r5.anchor: وقال في ( العارضة ) : لم يحقق العلماء تعيين النازل بمكة من النازل بالمدينة في الجملة ولا يحقق وقت إسلام ابن أم مكتوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r6.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī’s uncertainty is unfounded here because exegetes agree that the sura is Meccan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r6.anchor: وهو مخالف لاتفاق أهل التفسير على أنها مكية فلا محصل لكلام ابن العربي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r7.claim: It ranks twenty-fourth in revelation, after Sūrat al-Najm and before Sūrat al-Qadr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r7.anchor: وعدت الرابعة والعشرين في ترتيب نزول السور . نزلت بعد سورة ( والنجم ) وقبل سورة ( القدر )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r8.claim: Verse counters in Medina, Mecca, and Kufa count 42 verses; Basra counts 41, and Syria 40.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r8.anchor: وعدد آيها عند العادين من أهل المدينة وأهل مكة وأهل الكوفة اثنتان وأربعون ، وعند أهل البصرة إحدى وأربعون وعند أهل الشام أربعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r9.claim: This is the first sura in the middle section of al-Mufaṣṣal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r9.anchor: وهي أولى السور من أواسط المفصل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r10.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says the occasion of revelation will be given in the commentary on 80:1.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r10.anchor: وسبب نزولها يأتي ذكره عند قوله تعالى : { عبس وتولى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r11.claim: A central purpose is to teach the Prophet to weigh degrees of benefit and investigate hidden factors, so an obvious priority does not eclipse an equal or greater one; legal theorists likewise require a mujtahid to seek conflicting evidence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r11.anchor: تعليم الله رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم الموازنة بين مراتب المصالح ووجوب الاستقراء لخفياتها كيلا يفيت الاهتمام بالمهم منها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r12.claim: The sura contrasts rejecting polytheists with Muslims who pursue guidance, honors believers’ rank before God, and praises the Quran and teaching it to willing learners.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r12.anchor: والإشارة إلى اختلاف الحال بين المشركين المعرضين عن هدي الإسلام وبين المسلمين المقبلين على تتبع مواقعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r13.claim: It then describes Quraysh leaders’ intense resistance to the call, which occupied the Prophet and distracted him from Ibn Umm Maktūm’s request.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p101/r13.anchor: وانتقل من ذلك إلى وصف شدة الكفر من صناديد قريش بمكابرة الدعوة التي شغلت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الالتفات إلى رغبة ابن أم مكتوم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p26#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p26#2/r1.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p26#2/r1.claim: The commentators say Muhammad was trying to bring Utba b. Rabiʿa, Abu Jahl, Umayya and Ubayy sons of Khalaf to Islam when the blind Ibn Umm Maktum repeatedly asked to be taught; Muhammad showed displeasure, turned away, and the verses were revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p26#2/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوما يناجي عتبة بن ربيعة وأبا جهل بن هشام وأمية وأبيا ابني خلف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p26#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p26#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p26#2/r2.claim: Afterward the Prophet honored Ibn Umm Maktum and welcomed him as the person about whom his Lord had reproached him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p26#2/r2.anchor: فكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يكرمه بعد ذلك ويقول مرحبا بمن عاتبني فيه ربي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p26#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p26#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p26#2/r3.claim: Some, including Muqatil, say Ibn Umm Maktum came to embrace Islam, and the Prophet turned away while occupied with the leaders; the verses then came down.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p26#2/r3.anchor: وذهب قوم منهم مقاتل إلى أنه إنما جاء ليؤمن فأعرض عنه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم اشتغالا بالرؤساء فنزلت فيه هذه الآيات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p26#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p26#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p26#2/r4.claim: ʿAbasa means he frowned or scowled, while tawalla means he turned his face away.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p26#2/r4.anchor: ومعنى عبس قطب وكلح وتولى أعرض بوجهه

JISHUMI:v10p7280/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r1.claim: ʿAbasa and tawallā are past verbs; an jaʾahu means because he came.
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r1.anchor: (عبس وتولى) فعل ماض. (أن جاءه) لأن جاءه.

JISHUMI:v10p7280/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r4.speaker: الحسن وجماعة
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r4.claim: They say it was revealed when Ibn Umm Maktūm interrupted the Prophet's effort to convert Meccan leaders; the Prophet turned back to them and God rebuked him.
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r4.anchor: قيل: نزلت الآيات في عبد الله بن أم مكتوم أتى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، وهو يناجي عتبة بن ربيعة

JISHUMI:v10p7280/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r5.speaker: الحسن وجماعة
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r5.claim: Afterward the Prophet honored him, welcomed him as the man over whom his Lord reproached him, and asked his needs.
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r5.anchor: فكان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بعد ذلك يكرمه، وإذا رآه قال: مرحبا بمن عاتبني ربي فيه،

JISHUMI:v10p7280/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r6.speaker: أنس
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r6.claim: Anas says he saw Ibn Umm Maktūm at al-Qādisiyya in armor with a black banner.
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r6.anchor: قال أنس: رأيته يوم القادسية، عليه درع، ومعه راية سوداء.

JISHUMI:v10p7280/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd relates the saying that if the Messenger concealed revelation, he would have concealed this passage.
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد: كان يقال: لو كتم رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - شيئا من الوحي لكتم هذا.

JISHUMI:v10p7280/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r8.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك وابن زيد
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r8.claim: They identify the blind man as Ibn Umm Maktūm.
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r8.anchor: وقيل: الأعمى ابن أم مكتوم، عن ابن عباس، والحسن، ومجاهد، وقتادة، والضحاك، وابن زيد.

JISHUMI:v10p7280/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r11.claim: The verse itself does not establish the incident concerns the Messenger; reports are solitary, not mass-transmitted.
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r11.anchor: وليس في ظاهر الآية ما يدل على أنه نزل في رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، ولا تواترت به الأخبار،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r1.claim: The occasion report says Ibn Umm Maktūm approached while the Prophet urged Quraysh leaders to accept Islam; the blind man repeatedly asked for teaching, and the Prophet frowned and turned away while occupied with them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r1.anchor: أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ابن أم مكتوم وأم مكتوم أم أبيه ، واسمه عبد الله بن شريح ابن مالك بن ربيعة الفهري

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r2.claim: The report identifies Ibn Umm Maktūm as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shurayḥ ibn Mālik ibn Rabīʿa al-Fihrī; Umm Maktūm was his mother’s name.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r2.anchor: وعنده صناديد قريش : عتبة وشيبة ابنا ربيعة ، وأبو جهل بن هشام . والعباس بن عبد المطلب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r3.claim: After the revelation, the Prophet honored Ibn Umm Maktūm, welcomed him as the one for whom his Lord had reproached him, asked about his needs, and twice appointed him over Medina.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r3.anchor: فكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يكرمه ويقول إذا رآه : مرحبا بمن عاتبني فيه ربي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r4.speaker: أنس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r4.claim: Anas says he saw Ibn Umm Maktūm at al-Qādisiyya wearing armor and carrying a black banner.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r4.anchor: وقال أنس : رأيته يوم القادسية وعليه درع وله راية سوداء .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r5.claim: A doubled sīn reading intensifies the meaning of ‘he frowned.’

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r6.claim: Depending on the grammatical analysis, an jāʾahu is governed by tawallā or by ʿabasa.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r6.anchor: أن جآءه } منصوب بتولى ، أو بعبس ، على اختلاف المذهبين .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r7.claim: A reading has two hamzas with an alif between them; pausing after ‘he frowned and turned away’ then beginning ‘because the blind man came?’ makes it an explicit rebuke.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r7.anchor: وقرىء ( أن جاءه ) بهمزتين وبألف بينهما ، ووقف على { عبس وتولى } ثم ابتديء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r8.claim: A report says that afterward the Prophet never again frowned at a poor person or turned his attention toward a rich one.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r8.anchor: وروى أنه ما عبس بعدها في وجه فقير قط ، ولا تصدى لغني .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r9.claim: Reporting the lapse first and then directly addressing the Prophet heightens the censure, like publicly complaining about a wrong before confronting its perpetrator.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r9.anchor: وفي الإخبار عما فرط منه ، ثم الإقبال عليه بالخطاب : دليل على زيادة الإنكار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r10.claim: Mentioning the blind man underscores the reproach: if his blindness seemed to warrant turning away, it should instead have inspired greater compassion, welcome, and closeness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r10.anchor: وفي ذكر الأعمى نحو من ذلك ، كأنه يقول : قد استحق عنده العبوس والإعراض لأنه أعمى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r11.speaker: سفيان الثوري
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r11.claim: Sufyān al-Thawrī is reported to have said that poor people were the leaders in his gatherings, reflecting the good etiquette people learned from this verse.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r11.anchor: فقد روي عن سفيان الثوري رحمه الله أن الفقراء كانوا في مجلسه أمراء

NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#8/r1.claim: The Prophet frowned and turned away.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#8/r1.anchor: ﴿ عبس ﴾ كلح أى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم ﴿ وتولى ﴾ أعرض

BURSEVI:v10p258/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p258/r3.speaker: السهيلي
BURSEVI:v10p258/r3.claim: Al-Suhaylī observes that the passage first reports the incident in third person, then turns to direct address, mirroring the Prophet’s initial turning away before addressing him to console him.
BURSEVI:v10p258/r3.anchor: قال الامام السهيلي رحمه الله ، انظر كيف نزلت الآية بلفظ الأخبار عن الغائب

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r1.claim: ʿAbasa means he frowned or scowled; basara is also used.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r1.anchor: { عبس } أي كلح بوجهه يقال: عبس وبسر.

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r2.claim: Tawalla means he turned his face away.

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r4.claim: Exegetes say Quraysh nobles were with the Prophet, whose hope of their conversion led him to focus on them; when Ibn Umm Maktum arrived, he turned away so as not to interrupt.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r4.anchor: فروى أهل التفسير أجمع أن قوما من أشراف قريش كانوا عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد طمع في إسلامهم، فأقبل عبد الله بن أم مكتوم

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r7.claim: The verse is God's reproach to the Prophet for turning away from ʿAbdullah ibn Umm Maktum.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r7.anchor: الثانية الآية عتاب من الله لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم في إعراضه وتوليه عن عبد الله بن أم مكتوم.

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r9.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r9.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi says Maliki scholars identify the prominent man as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, known by the kunya Abu ʿAbd Shams.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r9.anchor: ابن العربي: قاله المالكية من علمائنا، وهو يكني أبا عبد شمس.

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r10.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r10.claim: Qatada identifies the man as Umayya ibn Khalaf; another report from him names Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r10.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو أمية بن خلص وعنه: أبي بن خلف.

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r11.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r11.claim: Mujahid says there were three men: ʿUtba and Shayba, sons of Rabiʿa, and Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد: كانوا ثلاثة عتبة وشيبة ابنا ربيعة وأبي بن خلف.

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r12.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r12.claim: ʿAta identifies the prominent man as ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa.

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r13.speaker: سفيان الثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r13.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri says the Prophet was speaking with his uncle al-ʿAbbas.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r13.anchor: سفيان الثوري: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مع عمه العباس.

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r14.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r14.claim: Al-Zamakhshari names ʿUtba, Shayba, Abu Jahl, al-ʿAbbas, Umayya, and al-Walid as Quraysh leaders; the Prophet sought their conversion hoping others would follow.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r14.anchor: الزمخشري: كان عنده صناديد قريش: عتبة وشيبة ابنا ربيعة، أبو جهل بن هشام، والعباس بن عبد المطلب

QASHANI:80:1/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:80:1/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:80:1/r1.claim: The Prophet was under his Lord’s nurturing; when his self manifested, it veiled him from the light of truth, so he acted from himself rather than through God.
QASHANI:80:1/r1.anchor: فكلما ظهرت نفسه بصفة حجبت عنه نور الحق حتى تحرك بنفسه لا بالله

QASHANI:80:1/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:80:1/r2.speaker: النبي
QASHANI:80:1/r2.claim: Qashani cites the Prophet’s saying, “My Lord disciplined me and perfected my discipline,” to frame the rebuke as divine education.
QASHANI:80:1/r2.anchor: كان صلى الله عليه وسلم في حجر تربية ربه لكونه حبيبا

QASHANI:80:1/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:80:1/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:80:1/r3.claim: Adoption of God’s qualities comes after arrival, annihilation, and realization in abiding; this is steadiness at spiritual establishment without fluctuation.
QASHANI:80:1/r3.anchor: فإن التخلق بأخلاقه كان بعد الوصول والفناء والتحقق به حال البقاء وهو الاستقامة وقت التمكين وانتفاء التلوين

QASHANI:80:1/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:80:1/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:80:1/r4.claim: He looked at outward status, esteemed wealthy leaders, and turned from the poor man, hoping the leaders might strengthen Islam if they believed and slighting the poor man’s faith.
QASHANI:80:1/r4.anchor: اعتناء بالقوم وتقوى الإسلام بهم إن آمنوا

QASHANI:80:1/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:80:1/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:80:1/r5.claim: The admonition is that a spiritual guide must not neglect a prepared, weak seeker for a wealthy, powerful person.
QASHANI:80:1/r5.anchor: نبه بأن مثلك لا ينبغي أن ينظر إلى ظاهر الحال فيتشاغل عن المستعد الطالب الضعيف بالغني القوي

QASHANI:80:1/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:80:1/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:80:1/r6.claim: Judgment should focus only on readiness and acceptance of faith, not outward appearances that veil the inward state.
QASHANI:80:1/r6.anchor: بل يجب أن يكون نظرك مقصورا على الاستعداد وقبول الإيمان فتعتبر ذلك دون غيره ولا تحتجب بالظاهر عن الباطن

QASHANI:80:1/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:80:1/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:80:1/r7.claim: The overlooked poor man may purify and adorn himself until reaching perfection and becoming a guide to others.
QASHANI:80:1/r7.anchor: عسى أن يكون الفقير المتلهى عنه عاملا بالتزكية والتحلية

QASHANI:80:1/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:80:1/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:80:1/r8.claim: The rich man he approached may fail to believe because he lacks readiness or is arrogant and obstinate.
QASHANI:80:1/r8.anchor: والغني المتصدى له لم يؤمن لعدم استعداده أو لاستكباره وعناده

RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r1.claim: Rāzī says Ibn Umm Maktūm (ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shurayḥ ibn Mālik) came while Muḥammad called ʿUtba and Shayba, Abū Jahl, al-ʿAbbās, Umayya, and al-Walīd to Islam; after repeated requests for teaching, the Prophet frowned and turned away, and the verse was revealed.
RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r1.anchor: أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ابن أم مكتوم وأم مكتوم أم أبيه واسمه عبدالله بن شريح بن مالك بن ربيعة الفهري

RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r2.claim: Rāzī adds that the Prophet honored Ibn Umm Maktūm, greeting him as the man for whom his Lord reproached him, asking his needs, and appointing him over Medina twice.
RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r2.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يكرمه

RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r3.claim: Rāzī raises the objection that Ibn Umm Maktūm deserved rebuke: despite blindness he heard the conversation, knew the Prophet’s concern, and interrupted before it ended, harming him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r3.anchor: ابن أم مكتوم كان يستحق التأديب والزجر

RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r4.claim: The objection adds that the already Muslim Ibn Umm Maktūm knew his religious needs, while conversion of the unbelieving chiefs might lead many others to Islam; interruption sacrificed a greater good.

RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r5.claim: The objection invokes 49:4: if calling the Prophet from behind chambers at the wrong time is censured, an interruption that diverts unbelievers from faith and blocks his chief mission seems worse.
RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r5.anchor: الذين ينادونك من وراء الحجرات أكثرهم لا يعقلون

RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r6.claim: The objection concludes that Ibn’s interruption was sinful and the Prophet’s action was required, then asks why God reproached the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v31p50/r6.anchor: فثبت بهذا أن الذي فعله ابن أم مكتوم

RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r1.claim: A second objection says that reproaching the Prophet for merely frowning greatly honors Ibn Umm Maktūm, so calling him “the blind” seems degrading.
RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r1.anchor: عاتبه على مجرد أنه عبس في وجهه

RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r2.claim: A third objection says the Prophet was authorized to discipline and teach his companions according to what he judged beneficial, so the frown seems to have been permitted.
RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r2.anchor: الظاهر أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان مأذونا في أن يعامل أصحابه على حسب ما يراه مصلحة

RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r3.claim: One answer is that the outward scene appeared to privilege the rich over the poor and break poor believers’ hearts; Rāzī compares it with 6:52.
RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r3.anchor: ظاهر الواقعة يوهم تقديم الأغنياء على الفقراء

RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r4.claim: Alternatively, the rebuke may concern an inward inclination toward the nobles for kinship and rank and aversion to the blind man for his lack of kinship and status, not the outward act itself.
RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r4.anchor: لعل هذا العتاب لم يقع على ما صدر من الرسول

RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r5.claim: Calling him blind is not belittling: his blindness is precisely why he deserved greater kindness and compassion.
RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r5.anchor: ذكره بلفظ الأعمى ليس لتحقير شأنه

RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r6.claim: Though the Prophet could discipline his companions, this incident seemed to place the wealthy before the poor and worldly concerns before religion, so it prompted the rebuke.
RAZI-FULL:v31p51/r6.anchor: كان مأذونا في تأديب أصحابه لكن ههنا لما أوهم

RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r1.speaker: القائلون بصدور الذنب عن الأنبياء
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r1.claim: Those who allow prophets to sin infer from God's reproach that the Prophet's act here was sinful.
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r1.anchor: القائلون بصدور الذنب عن الأنبياء عليهم السلام تمسكوا بهذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī says the act was required in that circumstance and at most resembled leaving caution or the preferable; it was not a sin.

RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r3.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r3.claim: Exegetes agree that the one who frowned and turned away was the Messenger, and that the blind man was Ibn Umm Maktum.
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r3.anchor: أجمع المفسرون على أن الذي عبس وتولى ، هو الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام ، وأجمعوا

RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r4.claim: A doubled reading of ʿabasa intensifies the sense, as in the doubled form kallaḥa.
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r4.anchor: وقرىء عبس بالتشديد للمبالغة ونحوه كلح في / كلح

RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r5.claim: The accusative phrase an jāʾahu is governed either by the nearer tawallā or the farther ʿabasa, according to differing rules about which governor acts.
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r5.anchor: أن جاءه منصوب بتولى أو بعبس على اختلاف المذهبين في إعمال الأقرب أو الأبعد

RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r6.claim: A reading with two hamzas and an intervening alif pauses after ʿabasa wa-tawallā, then begins as a reproach: the blind man has now come.
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r6.anchor: وقرىء أن جاءه بهمزتين ، وبألف بينهما وقف على { عبس وتولى } ثم ابتدأ

RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r7.claim: The shift from reporting the Prophet's lapse in the third person to addressing him directly heightens reproach, like publicly complaining and then confronting the offender.
RAZI-FULL:v31p51#2/r7.anchor: الإقبال عليه بالخطاب دليل على زيادة الإنكار

SULAMI:v2p373#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p373#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p373#2/r1.claim: Some say God gently rebuked the Prophet regarding the sincere poor, thereby honoring the station of poverty and magnifying its people.
SULAMI:v2p373#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم في قوله : ﴿ عبس وتولى أن جاءه الأعمى ﴾ عاتب الله نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بألطف عتاب

TABRISI:80:20/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r6.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:80:20/r6.claim: The passage is said to have been revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum, also named Abdullah ibn Shurayh ibn Malik ibn Rabiʿa al-Fihri, when he came as the Prophet was urging Quraysh leaders toward Islam.
TABRISI:80:20/r6.anchor: قيل نزلت الآيات في عبد الله بن أم مكتوم وهو عبد الله بن شريح بن مالك ابن ربيعة الفهري

TABRISI:80:20/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r7.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:80:20/r7.claim: The Prophet was speaking with ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa, Abu Jahl, al-ʿAbbas, Ubayy, and Umayya ibn Khalaf when Ibn Umm Maktum repeatedly asked to be taught; the Prophet turned away, thinking the leaders might scorn a following of blind people and slaves.
TABRISI:80:20/r7.anchor: وذلك أنه أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يناجي عتبة بن ربيعة وأبا جهل بن هشام والعباس بن عبد المطلب وأبيا وأمية ابني خلف

TABRISI:80:20/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:80:20/r8.claim: Afterward the Prophet honored Ibn Umm Maktum, greeted him as the man for whom his Lord had reproached him, asked about his needs, and appointed him deputy in Medina twice.
TABRISI:80:20/r8.anchor: وكان رسول الله بعد ذلك يكرمه

TABRISI:80:20/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r9.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TABRISI:80:20/r9.claim: Anas ibn Malik says he saw Ibn Umm Maktum at al-Qadisiyya wearing armor and carrying a black standard.
TABRISI:80:20/r9.anchor: وقال أنس بن مالك: فرأيته يوم القادسية وعليه درع ومعه راية سوداء

TABRISI:80:20/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r10.speaker: المرتضى علم الهدى
TABRISI:80:20/r10.claim: Al-Murtada rejects identifying the passage's subject as the Prophet: the text does not name him, and frowning at a believing seeker or preferring rich people to the poor conflicts with his noble character.
TABRISI:80:20/r10.anchor: قال المرتضى علم الهدى قدس الله روحه: ليس في ظاهر الآية دلالة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p209#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p209#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p209#2/r1.claim: The one who frowned was the Prophet.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p209#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p209#2/r4.speaker: جماعة المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p209#2/r4.claim: Ibn Umm Maktum came while the Prophet was urging Quraysh nobles toward God and Islam; he repeatedly asked to be taught Qur’an, unaware the Prophet was occupied. The Prophet frowned, turned away, and these verses were revealed.

STUDYQURAN:80:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:1/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:80:1/r1.claim: The Prophet is admonished for turning from a guidance seeker toward people he hoped to attract to Islam.
STUDYQURAN:80:1/r1.anchor: The Prophet is here admonished for turning away from one who sought guidance to others whom he hoped to attract to Islam

STUDYQURAN:80:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:1/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:80:1/r2.claim: The Prophet could not make people accept religion; his role was to convey God's message and guide those who accepted it.
STUDYQURAN:80:1/r2.anchor: he was not responsible for making people accept religion, only for conveying God’s message and guiding those who accepted it

STUDYQURAN:80:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:1/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:80:1/r3.claim: Other verses instruct the Prophet to be patient and not turn away from people seeking religion.
STUDYQURAN:80:1/r3.anchor: Other verses tell the Prophet to be patient and to not turn away from those who seek religion

TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r4.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r4.claim: Aisha says the passage was revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum, who asked the Prophet for guidance while he was with leading polytheists; the Prophet turned toward them and away from him.
TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r4.anchor: عن عائشة، قالت: أنزلت {عبس وتولى} [عبس: 1] في ابن أم مكتوم

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r1.speaker: طرق أهل السنة
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r1.claim: Sunni reports say these verses came when blind Ibn Umm Maktūm entered while the Prophet spoke with Quraysh leaders about Islam; the Prophet frowned, and God reproached him.
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r1.anchor: من طرق أهل السنة أن الآيات نزلت في قصة ابن أم مكتوم الأعمى دخل على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r2.speaker: طرق الشيعة
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r2.claim: Some Shiʿi reports also point to Ibn Umm Maktūm's entry and the Prophet's frowning.
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r2.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار من طرق الشيعة إشارة إلى ذلك

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r3.speaker: بعض روايات الشيعة
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r3.claim: Other Shiʿi reports say the person who frowned was an Umayyad man with the Prophet; he tightened his face when Ibn Umm Maktūm entered.
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r3.anchor: وفي بعض روايات الشيعة أن العابس المتولي رجل من بني أمية كان عند النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r4.claim: The sūra rebukes preferring the wealthy and privileged to poor believers, then recalls human dependence on God's care despite ingratitude and turns to resurrection, recompense, and warning.
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r4.anchor: فغرض السورة عتاب من يقدم الأغنياء والمترفين على الضعفاء والمساكين من المؤمنين فيرفع أهل الدنيا ويضع أهل الآخرة

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r6.claim: ʿAbasa means he frowned or tightened his face, and tawallā means he turned away.

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r11.claim: The first two verses speak in the third person, distancing the rebuke; the next two switch to direct address, intensifying reproach and accountability.
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r11.anchor: ويزيد شدة بإتيان الآيتين الأوليين في سياق الغيبة لما فيه من الإعراض عن المشافهة والدلالة على تشديد الإنكار

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r13.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r13.claim: On the view that the Prophet is the one reproached, third-person wording honors him by implying someone else acted; the later direct address also honors him through intimacy after estrangement.
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r13.anchor: وقيل - بناء على كون المراد بالمعاتب هو النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم - أن في التعبير عنه أولا بضمير الغيبة إجلالا له

TABATABAI:80:13-16/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:13-16/r12.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:80:13-16/r12.claim: Al-Majmaʿ recounts that Abdullah ibn Shurayḥ ibn Mālik ibn Rabīʿa al-Fihri, Ibn Umm Maktūm, interrupted the Prophet's appeal to ʿUtba, Abū Jahl, al-ʿAbbās, Ubayy, and Umayya ibn Khalaf to ask for teaching; the Prophet frowned, fearing the elites would scorn followers who were blind or enslaved, then turned back to them.
TABATABAI:80:13-16/r12.anchor: في المجمع قيل نزلت الآيات في عبد الله بن أم مكتوم وهو عبد الله بن شريح بن مالك بن ربيعة الفهروي

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r1.claim: Because the Prophet is described as possessing tremendous character and not harshness, the apparent subject of عبس وتولى may be someone else.

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r2.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r2.claim: Al-Sadiq reports that the passage was revealed about an Umayyad man with the Prophet who scowled and turned away when Ibn Umm Maktum arrived.
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r2.anchor: روي عن الصادق ع أنها نزلت في رجل من بني أمية كان عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r3.claim: If the passage concerns the Prophet, scowling at a blind man is not sinful because he cannot see it; God may still admonish the Prophet toward the highest manners and prioritize guiding a believer over courting a polytheist.
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r3.anchor: فالجواب أن العبوس والانبساط مع الأعمى سواء إذ لا يشق عليه

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r4.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r4.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi says an act may become sinful through a later prohibition, but its earlier occurrence was not thereby sinful; the prohibition came only now.
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r4.anchor: وقال الجبائي: في هذا دلالة على أن الفعل يكون معصية

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r5.claim: Another view says Ibn Umm Maktum behaved discourteously and deserved to be ignored, but God rebuked the response because he might think poverty caused the rejection and status won the leaders’ welcome.
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r5.anchor: إن ما فعله الأعمى نوعا من سوء الأدب فحسن تأديبه بالإعراض عنه

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r6.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r6.claim: Al-Sadiq reports that the Prophet welcomed Ibn Umm Maktum warmly, saying God would never rebuke him on his account, and treated him with such kindness that he restrained himself for the Prophet.
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r6.anchor: وروي عن الصادق ع أنه قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r7.claim: عبس means to frown or contract the face, and تولى means to turn one’s face away.

BURSEVI:v10p257/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p257/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p257/r1.claim: Bursevī reports that Sūrat ʿAbasa is Meccan and counted as either forty or forty-one verses.
BURSEVI:v10p257/r1.anchor: أربعون أو إحدى وأربعون آية مكية

BURSEVI:v10p257/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p257/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p257/r2.claim: ʿAbasa describes a frowning or sour expression, while tawallā means that he turned away.
BURSEVI:v10p257/r2.anchor: العبس والعبوس ترش روى شدن يعني ترش كرد روى خودرا

THALABI:v10p130#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p130#3/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p130#3/r1.claim: “ʿAbasa” means he frowned, and “tawallā” means he turned away with his face.
THALABI:v10p130#3/r1.anchor: عبس كلح. وتولى وأعرض عنه بوجهه

THALABI:v10p130#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p130#3/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p130#3/r2.claim: Ibn Umm Maktum repeatedly asked for instruction while the Prophet addressed Quraysh leaders; the Prophet turned from him, thinking the elite might reject a following of blind, poor, and enslaved people.
THALABI:v10p130#3/r2.anchor: أنه أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يناجي عتبة بن ربيعة وأبا جهل بن هشام

THALABI:v10p130#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p130#3/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v10p130#3/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says it was said that, had the Prophet concealed any revelation, he would have concealed these verses.
THALABI:v10p130#3/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد كان يقال: لو كتم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شيئا من الوحي لكتم هذا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:1-5/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:1-5/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:1-5/r1.claim: The Prophet frowned and turned away.

ELMALILI:80:1-2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r1.claim: ʿAbasa and ʿubūs mean twisting the face in discomfort: to sour one’s expression, curl the nose, or grimace.
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r1.anchor: “Abs” ve “ubûs”, bîhuzurluktan yüz burkulmak mânasınadır ki yüz ekşimek, burun

ELMALILI:80:1-2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r2.speaker: Kāmûs şârihi
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r2.claim: The verb can also be transitive, meaning to make a face or frown.
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r2.anchor: Kāmûs şârihinin beyânına göre müte‘addî olarak da kullanılır ki yüz ekşitmek, surat etmek

ELMALILI:80:1-2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r3.claim: With wajh nominative, the expression means “his face frowned”; with wajh accusative, it means “he frowned his face.”
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r3.anchor: Lâzım olarak عَبَسَ وَجْهُهُ denilir, “yüzü[^2] ekşidi” demek olur. Müte‘addî olarak da “vech”in nasbıyla عَبَسَ وَجْهَهُ

ELMALILI:80:1-2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r4.claim: Turkish ekşime/ekşitme likely evokes the face’s contraction after tasting something sour or bitter.
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r4.anchor: Bizim buna “ekşime” veya “ekşitme” tâbir etmemiz pek ekşi veya buruk bir şey yenildiği zaman yüzü bu hâlde buruşturması münasebetiyle olmalıdır.

ELMALILI:80:1-2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r5.claim: Although “face” is often named, Turkish may omit it; saying someone ekşidi when another arrives means he disliked that person’s coming, as here.
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r5.anchor: Burada da böyle yüz zikredilmeyerek عَبَسَ buyurulmuştur. Yani hoşlanmadı, ekşidi

ELMALILI:80:1-2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r6.claim: Tawallā means that he turned away, refused, or turned in another direction.
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r6.anchor: {وَتَوَلَّىٰٓ} ve döndü i‘râz etti, öte yöneldi

ELMALILI:80:1-2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r8.claim: To show that frowning and turning away from such people is improper, the passage shifts from an absent third-person rebuke to direct address and from outward appearance to inward meaning.
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r8.anchor: Bu gibilerden ubûs ve i‘râzın lâyık olmadığını beyan için gıyâbî itabdan hitâba ve zâhirden bâtına geçilerek buyuruluyor ki

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r1.claim: The Prophet was speaking with pagan leaders, hoping their conversion would make the public follow; when Ibn Umm Maktum arrived with a question, the Prophet frowned and did not answer, prompting God’s rebuke.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r1.anchor: Hz. Peygamber putperest önderlerin ikna edilmesi halinde onları izleyen halkın İslâm’ı daha kolay benimseyecekleri düşüncesiyle onlarla da meşgul oluyordu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r2.claim: A report says the Prophet later greeted Abdullah with affection, saying, “Welcome to the man on whose account my Lord reproached me.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r2.anchor: “Kendisinden dolayı rabbimin beni azarladığı şahsa merhaba!” diyerek ona iltifatta bulunduğu rivayet edilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r3.claim: Zamakhshari reports that the Prophet twice appointed Abdullah to lead prayers in Medina when he left on campaign.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r3.anchor: sefere çıktığında iki defa yerine Medine’de kalanlara namaz kıldırmak üzere Abdullah’ı görevlendirdiği de rivayet edilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r4.claim: The Qur’an recalls and corrects several prophetic slips; for a similar admonition, the commentary points to 9:43, while these verses alone use a comparatively stern tone.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r4.anchor: Birkaç âyette Hz. Peygamber’in “zelle” denilen bazı hataları hatırlatılmış ve düzeltilmiştir (meselâ buna yakın bir uyarı örneği için bk. Tevbe 9/43)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r5.claim: The rebuke shows revelation’s objectivity: the Prophet conveyed God’s revelation rather than his own wishes and should not be treated as a deity incapable of error.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r5.anchor: vahyin objektifliğini ve peygamberin insanlığa kendi istek ve düşüncelerini değil, ilâhî vahyi tebliğ ettiğini, ayrıca onun bir ilâh gibi yanılgısız sayılmaması gerektiğini göstermesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r6.claim: The Prophet publicly recited verses criticizing his own conduct without anxiety or defensiveness, demonstrating sincerity in his mission, love of truth, and excellent character.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r6.anchor: Resûlullah’ın, kendi tutumunu eleştiren bu âyetleri, en ufak bir kaygı ve komplekse kapılmadan halka okuması, duyurması

BURHAN:v2p242/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p242/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v2p242/r5.claim: Some say the person who frowned was Umayya, not Muhammad, since the verse uses third person rather than saying you frowned.
BURHAN:v2p242/r5.anchor: وقوله ﴿ عبس وتولى ﴾ قيل إنه امية

BURHAN:v2p242/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p242/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p242/r7.claim: The author's resolution is that such speech addresses the public without intending a particular person, in keeping with all revealed laws.
BURHAN:v2p242/r7.anchor: والتحقيق ان هذا ونحوه من باب خطاب العام من غير قصد شخص معين والمعنى اتفاق جميع الشرائع على ذلك

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r1.claim: God's noble name opens generosity to believers; the mighty name remains beyond the reach of all who seek to find it.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r1.anchor: ^ ( بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ) ^ ' بسم الله ' اسم كريم بسط للمؤمنين بساط جوده

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r2.claim: God cannot be comprehended through time or place, and humans know and remember Him only through Him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r2.anchor: من الذي يعرفه إلا وبه يعرفه ؟ ومن الذي يذكره إلا وبه يذكره ؟

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r3.claim: The passage was revealed about the blind Ibn Umm Maktum, who arrived while the Prophet spoke with al-Abbas and Umayya ibn Khalaf, hoping they would believe; the Prophet did not interrupt them, turned away, and frowned.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r3.anchor: نزلت في ابن أم مكتوم ، وكان ضريرا . . أتى النبي وكان عنده العباس بن عبد المطلب

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r4.claim: A tafsir report says the Prophet followed Ibn Umm Maktum and sent someone to find him afterward.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r4.anchor: وجاء في التفسير : أن النبي خرج على أثره ، وأمر بطلبه

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r5.claim: The same tafsir account says the Prophet thereafter honored Ibn Umm Maktum and appointed him to govern Medina twice.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r5.anchor: وكان بعد ذلك يبره ويكرمه ، فاستخلفه على المدينة مرتين

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r6.claim: A tafsir report says that after this the Prophet never frowned at or turned away from a poor person.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r6.anchor: وجاء في التفسير : أنه لم يعبس - بعد هذا - في وجه فقير قط

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r7.claim: The address is tactful: it does not confront Ibn Umm Maktum directly, but speaks of him indirectly.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r7.anchor: ويقال : في الخطاب لطف . . . وهو أنه لم يواجهه بل قاله على الكناية

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r1.speaker: عائشة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r1.claim: Aisha says the opening of Surat ʿAbasa was revealed about the blind Ibn Umm Maktum, who came seeking guidance while the Prophet attended to a leading polytheist and turned away from him.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r1.anchor: أخرج الترمذي والحاكم عن عائشة قالت أنزل ﴿ عبس وتولى ﴾ في ابن أم مكتوم الأعمى

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r2.speaker: أنس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r2.claim: Anas also transmitted a similar report that these verses were revealed about the blind Ibn Umm Maktum’s encounter with the Prophet.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r2.anchor: وأخرج أبو يعلى مثله عن أنس

FARRA:v3p235/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p235/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p235/r1.claim: The blind man was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm, whose paternal grandmother was Umm Maktūm; he came to ask the Prophet useful questions while Quraysh notables were present, and the Prophet disliked interrupting his conversation, prompting the revelation.
FARRA:v3p235/r1.anchor: ذلك عبد الله بن أم مكتوم وكانت أم مكتوم أم أبيه آتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

FARRA:v3p235/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p235/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p235/r2.anchor: يعني: محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

NAHHAS:v5p149/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p149/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p149/r1.claim: The form عبّس is used for intensification.

SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r5.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads عبس with a doubled ب.
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r5.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي " عبس " بالتشديد

ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r2.claim: The passage was revealed about ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm, who came while the Prophet was calling Quraysh notables to Islam, hoping their conversion would draw others.
ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r2.anchor: نزلت في عبد الله ابن أم مكتوم

ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r3.claim: The Prophet turned from Ibn Umm Maktūm to address the notables, so God instructed him not to neglect a Muslim by attending to someone else.
ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r3.anchor: فأمره الله ألا يتشاغل عن الإقبال على أحد من المسلمين بغيره

ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r4.claim: Asad argues that conduct amounting to minor discourtesy in an ordinary person became a major sin deserving divine rebuke when committed by a prophet.
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r4.anchor: what would have been a minor act of discourtesy on the part of an ordinary human being, assumed the aspect of a major sin

ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r5.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r5.claim: Asad says the use of third-person forms in verses 1–2 particularly sharpens the Qur'anic rebuke.
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r5.anchor: the sharp Qur'anic rebuke (stressed, in particular, by the use of the third-person form in verses 1-2)

ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r6.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r6.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r6.claim: Asad takes the Prophet's public conveyance of God's reproof as evidence that revelation is objective, connecting it to 53:3.
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r6.anchor: in conveying God's reproof of him to the world at large, the Prophet "does not speak out of his own desire" (cf. 53:3)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p197/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p197/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p197/r2.claim: The Resurrection flight scene belongs in Abasa, which opens with turning away: turning aside is a kind of flight, frowning is inward flight from something, and being distracted from the seeker is another form of it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p197/r2.anchor: والتولي نوع من أنواع الفرار من الشيء والانصراف عنه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.claim: ʿAbasa pairs with al-Nāziʿāt and shares its central theme, discourse style, and reasoning; the changed sequence of topics gives this sūrah its distinct majesty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.anchor: There is no basic difference between the central theme of both sūrahs.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r2.claim: Al-Nāziʿāt ends by calling the Prophet a warner for those who fear Judgment; ʿAbasa opens by rebuking him for attending to arrogant Quraysh leaders who demand the poor companions be turned away.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r2.anchor: you are but a warner for people who fear it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r3.claim: Though the Prophet is addressed in the rebuke, its intended target is the haughty leaders who ignore his message and want poor companions excluded to secure their own attendance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r3.anchor: Although the Prophet (sws) is addressed, yet the direction of this stern address is towards these supercilious people.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r4.claim: The Prophet's responsibility is to teach those who come eagerly, including devoted companions, rather than pamper absent leaders; he is not accountable for those who refuse to come.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r4.anchor: His real responsibility is to educate and instruct only those who come to him enthusiastically.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r1.claim: The occasion report says Ibn Umm Maktūm came while the Prophet was speaking with Quraysh leaders to invite them to Islam; unaware of the conversation, he repeatedly asked for instruction, and the Prophet frowned and turned away, prompting revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r1.anchor: روي أن ابن أم مكتوم وهو ابن خال خديجة واسمه عمرو بن قيس بن زائدة بن جندب بن هرم بن رواحة بن حجر بن معيص بن عامر بن لؤي القرشي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r5.claim: The Prophet later honored him, welcomed him as the man for whom his Lord had reproved him, asked about his needs, and appointed him to deputize in Medina; Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr reports that he led prayers there thirteen times.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r5.anchor: فكان رسول الله عليه الصلاة والسلام يكرمه ويقول إذا رآه مرحبا بمن عاتبني فيه ربي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r8.claim: The third-person pronoun for the Prophet honors him by making it seem that the deed came from someone else, since such conduct would not be expected of him.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r8.anchor: وضمير عبس وما بعده للنبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وفي التعبير عنه عليه الصلاة والسلام بضمير الغيبة إجلال له

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r1.claim: ʿAbasa means he frowned, and tawallā means he turned his face away.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r3.claim: The Prophet was inviting Utbah, Abu Jahl, al-Abbas, Ubayy ibn Khalaf, and Umayya to Islam when Ibn Umm Maktum repeatedly asked him to teach him; unaware of the others, the Prophet disliked the interruption, fearing the nobles would disparage his followers, so he frowned and turned away, and the verses were revealed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r3.anchor: وذلك أنه أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهو يناجي عتبة بن ربيعة، وأبا جهل بن هشام، والعباس بن عبد المطلب،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r4.claim: Afterward the Prophet honored Ibn Umm Maktum, welcomed him as the one about whom his Lord reproached him, asked his needs, and appointed him over Medina twice during campaigns.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r4.anchor: فكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد ذلك يكرمه، وإذا رآه قال: مرحبا بمن عاتبني فيه ربي،

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r1.claim: Surat Abasa is Meccan and has forty-two verses.

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r3.claim: A doubled reading intensifies the sense of frowning.
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r3.anchor: وقرىء «عبس» بالتشديد للمبالغة و { أن جاءه }

BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r1.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm, an early Muslim, interrupted the Prophet while he was seeking the conversion of Quraysh chiefs and their followers; the Prophet turned toward them, fearing the opportunity would be lost.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r1.anchor: وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين مجيئه مشتغلا بدعاء ناس من صناديد قريش إلى الله تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r2.claim: The sūra refers to the Prophet in the third person out of reverence, as Saʿd ibn Muʿādh also avoided addressing him directly when judging Banū Qurayẓa.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r2.anchor: معظما له صلى الله عليه وسلم بسياق الغيبة كما قال سعد بن معاذ رضي الله عنه لما حكم في بني قريظة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r3.claim: The frown was a human response to having his intended course blocked, though it ran against the Prophet’s divinely cultivated respect for the poor and joy in their company.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r3.anchor: فعل الكاره للشيء من تقطيب الوجه بما له من الطبع البشري حين يحال بينه وبين مراده

BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r4.claim: He turned away in the hope that the nobles would accept Islam and bring their numerous followers with them, advancing God’s cause.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r4.anchor: كلف نفسه الإعراض عنه رجاء أن يسلم أولئك الأشراف الذين كان يخاطبهم

DURR-FULL:v8p416/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r1.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r1.claim: Anas reports that Ibn Umm Maktum came while the Prophet spoke with Ubayy ibn Khalaf; the Prophet turned away, revelation followed, and he later honored Ibn Umm Maktum.
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r1.anchor: وأخرج عبد الرزاق وعبد بن حميد وأبو يعلى عن أنس قال: جاء ابن أم مكتوم إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v8p416/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet was urging ʿUtba, al-Abbas, and Abu Jahl toward Islam when Ibn Umm Maktum asked for instruction; he frowned and turned away, then later honored him.
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس قال: بينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يناجي عتبة بن ربيعة والعباس بن عبد المطلب

DURR-FULL:v8p416/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r3.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r3.claim: Abu Malik says Ibn Umm Maktum came while the Prophet courted Umayya ibn Khalaf, and the Prophet frowned and turned away.
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r3.anchor: وأخرج سعيد بن منصور وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر عن أبي مالك في قوله: {عبس وتولى} قال: جاءه عبد الله بن أم مكتوم

DURR-FULL:v8p416/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r4.speaker: الحكم
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r4.claim: Al-Hakam reports that after this revelation the Prophet was never seen courting a rich person or turning away from a poor one.
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r4.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن الحكم قال: ما رؤي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد هذه الآية متصديا لغني

DURR-FULL:v8p416/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says that if the Prophet had concealed revelation, he would have concealed this one about himself.
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن زيد قال: لو أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كتم شيئا من الوحي

DURR-FULL:v8p417/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r3.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says the Prophet was inviting a Quraysh notable to Islam when Ibn Umm Maktum asked questions; God reproached him, and he later honored Ibn Umm Maktum and appointed him governor of Medina twice.
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن سعد وابن المنذر عن الضحاك في قوله: {عبس وتولى} قال: هو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v8p417/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r4.speaker: مسروق
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r4.claim: Al-Hakim authenticated Masruq’s report from Aisha: Ibn Umm Maktum was the blind man, and the verse came when the Prophet was with ʿUtba and Shayba.
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r4.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم وصححه وابن مردويه في شعب الإيمان عن مسروق قال: دخلت على عائشة

DURR-FULL:v8p417/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r5.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet feared the Quraysh notable would think his followers were only blind, low-status people and slaves, so he disliked the interruption and frowned.
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r5.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن مجاهد قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مستخليا بصنديد من صناديد قريش

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r1.claim: The object of ‘turned away’ is omitted because the context makes clear that he turned away from the person whose arrival occasioned it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r1.anchor: وحذف متعلق { تولى } لظهور أنه تول عن الذي مجيئه كان سبب التولي .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r5.claim: The declarative wording rebukes a lapse in focus: the Prophet concentrated on delivering the message to likely converts while overlooking an already believing person eager to learn religion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r5.anchor: وصيغة الخبر مستعملة في العتاب على الغفلة عن المقصود الذي تضمنه الخبر وهو اقتصار النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على الاعتناء بالحرص على تبليغ الدعوة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r6.claim: God initially refers to the Prophet in the third person so the rebuke reaches him gradually rather than striking directly; the discourse later shifts to second-person address.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r6.anchor: فوجهه إليه على أسلوب الغيبة ليكون أول ما يقرع سمعه باعثا على أن يترقب المعني من ضمير الغائب فلا يفاجئه العتاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r7.claim: The indirect rebuke is compared with the verse that first says God has pardoned the Prophet before asking why he gave permission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r7.anchor: ونظير هذا قوله : { عفا الله عنك لم أذنت لهم } ( التوبة : 43 ) .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r8.speaker: عياض ناقلا عن عون بن عبد الله والسمرقندي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r8.claim: They report that God told the Prophet of his pardon before telling him of the lapse, calming his heart; Ibn ʿĀshūr compares this with the indirect rebuke here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r8.anchor: قال عياض : قال عون بن عبد الله والسمرقندي : أخبره الله بالعفو قبل أن يخبره بالذنب حتى سكن قلبه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r9.claim: The Prophet apparently hoped the gathered Quraysh leaders would accept Islam and bring most or all Quraysh with them; Ibn Umm Maktūm’s entrance interrupted the exchange as he repeatedly sought instruction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r9.anchor: ويظهر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رجا من ذلك المجلس أن يسلموا فيسلم بإسلامهم جمهور قريش أو جميعهم فكان دخول ابن أم مكتوم قطعا لسلك الحديث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r10.claim: The Prophet’s displeasure may have reflected the interruption and his concern that the gathered leaders would disperse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r10.anchor: فظهرت الكراهية في وجه الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم لعله لقطعه عليه كلامه وخشيته أن يفترق النفر المجتمعون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r1.claim: عبوس is a frown and darkening of the face when something is disliked.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r1.anchor: تقطب الوجه واربداده عند كراهية أمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r2.claim: Speaking of the addressee in the third person intensifies the reproach by conveying some disregard.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r2.anchor: وفي مخاطبته بلفظ ذكر الغائب مبالغة في العتب لأن في ذلك بعض الإعراض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r3.speaker: كثير من العلماء، ابن زيد، عائشة
